misconception_description: Student believes that a variable assigned an arithmetic expression containing other variables automatically updates its value when those variables change.

solutions.generated_code:
program HitungUmurAnjing
kamus
  umur : integer
  umurAnjing : real
algoritma
  input(umur)
  umurAnjing <- 21 + (umur - 2) * 4
  if umur <= 2 then
    umur <- 21 / 10.5
  endif
  output(umurAnjing)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student calculates d_age using the formula for older dogs (21 + (h_age - 2) * 4) first. Then, when they discover the dog is 2 years or younger, they attempt to "fix" the calculation by changing h_age to a value that would make the young dog formula work (setting h_age = 21 / 10.5 = 2). The student believes that because d_age was defined as an expression involving h_age, changing h_age will automatically cause d_age to update to the correct value. They don't realize they need to explicitly reassign d_age = h_age * 10.5. This results in returning the incorrect d_age value for young dogs (dogs 2 years or younger will get wrong ages returned).
